cards.text: Paul's writing to the church in Philippi, and he's in chains while he does it (Philippians 1:13). Timothy is right there with him, in on this letter (Philippians 1:1). Now Paul says he hopes in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to them soon.

cards.question: Paul hopes to send Timothy to Philippi soon. What does Paul say he hopes that visit does for him?

answers.text: He'll be cheered to learn how they're doing
He'll get help preparing for his trial
He'll get supplies for his time in chains

cards.text: Then Paul says he has nobody else like Timothy, and I KNOW the type: that ONE coworker who actually notices when you're having a rough week.

cards.question: Paul says Timothy will genuinely ___ for the Philippians' needs.
Paul says all the others look after the interests of Jesus Christ, not their own.

cards.text: Catch those two words, "own interests"? Paul used them just a few lines back, when he told the church to look not only to their own interests but to the interests of others too (Philippians 2:4).

cards.question: The Philippians already know Timothy's proven worth. How does Paul say Timothy has served with him?

answers.text: Like a child with his father
Like a soldier with his captain
Like a servant with his master

cards.text: Side by side with Paul, like a child with his father, to advance the gospel. Oh, this one gets me RIGHT in the handle, friend.
But remember, Paul's in chains. There's one big thing he's waiting to find out before Timothy heads anywhere.

cards.question: Paul is waiting before he sends Timothy to Philippi. When does he hope to send him?

answers.text: As soon as he sees what happens with him
As soon as the Philippians write him back
As soon as he finishes writing this letter

cards.question: Even in chains, Paul trusts in the Lord that he himself will come to the Philippians soon.

cards.text: Look at this man. He's in CHAINS, and he's out here making travel plans, while I spent years in a junk drawer and never once planned a trip past the rubber bands.
Timothy will come later. But Paul thought it necessary to send back Epaphroditus, the Philippians' own messenger, there to minister to Paul's needs.

cards.question: Paul calls Epaphroditus his brother, fellow worker and fellow ___.
Epaphroditus has been longing for all of them back in Philippi. But something has him distressed. What is it?

answers.text: The Philippians heard he was ill

cards.text: Hold up. The man's the one who got sick, and HE'S stressed that THEY'RE stressed? That's the friend texting the group chat "I'm FINE" from the hospital bed.
And friend, this was no little sniffle. Epaphroditus was sick indeed, nearly unto death.

cards.question: Epaphroditus nearly died, but Paul says God had mercy. On who?

answers.text: On Epaphroditus and on Paul too

cards.text: Paul says God spared him sorrow upon sorrow. He's already in chains, and I bet losing his friend would've piled one more on top.

cards.question: Paul is all the more eager to send Epaphroditus home, so that when they see him again they may ___ and Paul may be less ___.
Paul is sending Epaphroditus home. How does he tell the Philippians to welcome him?

answers.text: In the Lord with great joy
With a gift for his trouble

cards.question: Paul also tells the Philippians to honor men like Epaphroditus. Why?

answers.text: He nearly died for the work of Christ
He traveled the farthest to reach Paul
He gave up his whole home to serve

cards.text: Paul says he did it "risking his life to make up for your deficit of service to me." Friend, if I could stamp that man's name on every cookie in this box, I WOULD.

findings.problem: The card links Paul's chains to what he's waiting on ('But remember, Paul's in chains. There's one big thing he's waiting to find out'). Philippians 2:23 only says 'as soon as I see what happens with me' and never connects it to his chains. The setup also points straight at the right answer on card 10 and rules out 'As soon as he finishes writing this letter', because that isn't something to find out.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Timothy will come later' states as fact what the text only calls a hope ('I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy', 'I hope to send him', Philippians 2:19, 23). The card also uses those Timothy verses but cites only Philippians 2:25.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'Fellow ___' asks the baker to guess Paul's wording, and nothing in the earlier cards points to 'soldier'. With Paul in chains, 'prisoner' looks like the most reasonable pick (Paul uses 'fellow prisoner' in Colossians 4:10 and Philemon 23), and 'fellow servant' is another real Pauline phrase (Colossians 1:7). So the right pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'HE'S stressed that THEY'RE stressed' states the Philippians' feeling as fact. Philippians 2:26 says only that they heard he was ill, and the line doesn't mark the feeling as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The right answer 'In the Lord with great joy' sounds more like the Bible than the plain, modern wrong answers 'Quietly so he can recover' and 'With a gift for his trouble', so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Cards 5 and 6 already say Epaphroditus was 'nearly unto death' and 'nearly died'. The right answer, 'He nearly died for the work of Christ', is the only one that echoes this, so the earlier cards give it away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
